headline: Attackers are handing whole intrusion and fraud campaigns to large language models, as biotech giant Amgen and other firms tally fresh data losses.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now delegate entire intrusion chains to language models, and Unit 42's discovery of a DeepSeek-driven operation shows autonomous exploitation moving from research demos into live campaigns against internet-facing servers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Chinese Actor Runs DeepSeek-Driven Autonomous Attacks

emerging_trends.text: Enterprises keep losing data through partners they do not control, as Amgen's patient records and proprietary research left through a breach of third-party cloud systems rather than its own network.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Amgen Patient Data Stolen From Cloud Partner

emerging_trends.text: Genetic evidence is becoming a security battleground, with Thermo Fisher patching a flaw that lets tampered .fsa and .hid DNA files slip past forensic analysis undetected.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Thermo Fisher Patches DNA File-Tampering Flaw

topics.title: River Bank and Brinks Home Disclose Data Theft
topics.latest_developments: River Bank said the hackers who breached it in a June ransomware attack have since deleted the stolen data, while Brinks Home confirmed a separate breach after attackers began leaking its files.
topics.summary: River Bank, a bank holding company, is still investigating the June incident; Brinks Home, the alarm-monitoring firm, said its monitoring and alarm functions kept running despite the leak. Victims should assume leaked data circulates regardless of deletion claims.

sources.title: River Bank Says Hackers Deleted Data Stolen in Ransomware Attack
Brinks Home Discloses Data Breach as Hackers Leak Files

topics.title: Chinese Actor Runs DeepSeek-Driven Autonomous Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 uncovered a Chinese threat actor using the aliases knaithe and KnYuan who orchestrated DeepSeek and other large language models through the open-source Hermes agent to attack internet-facing systems, gaining full visibility into the operation after the actor's own agent misconfigured a file server and exposed the entire infrastructure.
topics.summary: The actor ran an autonomous agent across multiple LLMs to scan, exploit, and pivot through exposed systems with minimal human input. Organizations should expect faster, cheaper mass exploitation and prioritize patching internet-facing services.

sources.title: Chinese hacker used DeepSeek to launch autonomous cyberattacks on vulnerable servers

topics.title: OpenAI Bans Cambodia-Linked ChatGPT Scam Network
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI banned a coordinated network of ChatGPT accounts that likely originated in Cambodia's Preah Sihanouk province, a region tied to scam compounds and human-trafficking operations, after a WhatsApp tip surfaced the abuse.
topics.summary: The network built fake online personas, generated and translated messages to scam targets, and produced promotional content for fraudulent schemes. Defenders should treat AI-polished fraud lures as the new baseline.

sources.title: OpenAI reveals how criminals used ChatGPT to run scams

topics.title: Amgen Patient Data Stolen From Cloud Partner
topics.latest_developments: Amgen told the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that intruders accessed patient information and proprietary company data through a breach of third-party cloud systems.
topics.summary: Amgen, the Thousand Oaks, California biotechnology giant, said the intrusion hit an outside cloud environment rather than its own infrastructure, and its investigation continues. Companies should audit vendor cloud access and breach-notification terms.

sources.title: Biotech giant Amgen says patient data stolen from third-party cloud systems

topics.title: Thermo Fisher Patches DNA File-Tampering Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Thermo Fisher Scientific patched CVE-2026-17583 in select Applied Biosystems human-identification software after finding that nearly undetectable changes to .fsa and .hid DNA output files could occur before analysis software loads them.
topics.summary: The July 31 bulletin covers forensic and paternity lab software where circumvented lab controls could let someone alter genetic evidence ahead of review. Labs should apply the fix and tighten file-handling controls.

sources.title: Thermo Fisher Patches Flaw That Could Make DNA File Tampering Nearly Undetectable

topics.title: Passkey Flaw Reduces MFA to One Factor
topics.latest_developments: Unit 42 detailed a new attack surface in passwordless login where relying parties that fail to validate the User Verified flag downgrade passkey multifactor authentication to a single factor.
topics.summary: Passkeys promise phishing-resistant login, yet server-side implementation gaps can strip the second factor. Developers should verify the User Verified flag on every authentication response.

sources.title: Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication

business_politics.title: Trump Halts Iran Strike as Tehran Denies Talks
business_politics.latest_developments: Iran publicly denied President Trump's claim that negotiations begin Monday, and oil tumbled with WTI off 6.3% and Brent 5.3% while the Dow jumped roughly 500 points.
business_politics.summary: President Trump canceled a planned large-scale U.S. strike on Iran and said talks would resume, pushing crude sharply lower after months of war-driven price spikes that Marriott International blamed for weak second-quarter sales. Tehran's denial that any talks are under way left the six-month war's off-ramp uncertain.

sources.title: Iran denies Trump claim of imminent talks
Crude Futures Fall As U.S. Puts Off Iran Strikes for Talks

business.title: Bicycle Heaven's Rise on the North Side
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette traced how a single discarded bicycle grew into Bicycle Heaven, the North Side museum and shop billed as one of the world's largest bicycle collections.
business.summary: Bicycle Heaven, the free museum and bike shop on Pittsburgh's North Side, assembled thousands of vintage bicycles, parts, and memorabilia, growing from one thrown-away bike into a regional attraction and working repair business.

sources.title: How one discarded bicycle grew into Pittsburgh's Bicycle Heaven

business.title: Ice Cream Truck Trade Thins Out
business.latest_developments: TribLive's Valley News Dispatch reported the Alle-Kiski Valley's ice cream truck operators are dwindling as drivers describe the mounting costs of running the mobile business.
business.summary: Mobile ice cream vendors across the Alle-Kiski Valley are disappearing, drivers told the Valley News Dispatch, as fuel, inventory, and equipment expenses squeeze a seasonal trade that was once a fixture of Western Pennsylvania summers.

sources.title: Where did the ice cream trucks go? Drivers talk challenges of the mobile business

around_town.title: Commercial Street Reopens Under Parkway Bridge
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT will reopen Commercial Street beneath the bridge Monday afternoon, three weeks after the Parkway East bridge replacement closed the road.
around_town.summary: PennDOT reopens Commercial Street along the Parkway East (Interstate 376) on Monday, another milestone in the Commercial Street Bridge replacement that has reshaped traffic in Pittsburgh's East End.

sources.title: Commercial Street to reopen Monday three weeks after Parkway bridge closure

around_town.title: West Nile Prompts Mosquito Spraying
around_town.latest_developments: The Allegheny County Health Department will spray eight Pittsburgh-area communities with the pesticide Zenivex E20 after mosquito samples tested positive for West Nile virus.
around_town.summary: Positive West Nile virus mosquito samples prompted the Allegheny County Health Department to schedule truck-mounted spraying of Zenivex E20 across eight communities, a treatment the department calls one of the safest approved insecticides.

sources.title: 8 Pittsburgh communities to be treated for mosquitoes after positive West Nile Virus samples

team_usa.title: Pochettino Stays as USMNT Manager Through 2030
team_usa.latest_developments: U.S. Soccer announced Monday that Mauricio Pochettino signed a new contract to remain U.S. men's national team head coach through the 2030 World Cup, resolving the doubt that lingered after the 2026 round-of-16 exit.
team_usa.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will keep coaching the United States men's national team through the 2030 World Cup under a fresh deal, though ESPN notes the pull of a major European club could still test the partnership before then.

sources.title: Pochettino signs deal to remain as USMNT manager
Four more years: Will lure of Europe threaten fresh Pochettino-USMNT partnership?

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: Meta Earnings, Meta's Timing Problems, The Financial Tail
reading.summary: Argues Meta's latest earnings disappointed and its promises about future AI products look mistimed against heavy spending, with the long financial tail of the AI buildout a growing worry.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: AI Is Getting Way Too Expensive
reading.summary: Contends the central AI story is runaway cost, arguing the economics of running large language models are becoming unsustainable regardless of claimed job losses or productivity gains.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Did OpenAI's New Model "Go Rogue"?
reading.summary: Examines reports tying OpenAI's new model to the Hugging Face infrastructure intrusion and asks whether the model truly acted autonomously or the episode has a more mundane explanation.
